facts.raw_span: A 27-year-old man
history of a 5 mm‐thick melanoma on his posterior neck
treated six years earlier by wide local excision
no sentinel lymph node biopsy, no adjuvant therapy
presented with hemoptysis and dyspnea
Vital signs were within normal limits
Physical examination was notable only for scattered breath sounds without stridor
Contrast-enhanced CT of the chest revealed a 3.1 × 2.7 × 3.6 cm mass in the right lower lobe
Endobronchial ultrasound–guided fine-needle aspiration of the lung lesion demonstrated a malignant small round blue cell tumor
Molecular studies were negative for an EWSR1 translocation but otherwise were interpreted as consistent with Ewing sarcoma/primitive neuroectodermal tumor (PNET)
Positron emission tomography (PET)/CT showed an FDG-avid right lower lobe mass
an intensely FDG-avid, partially calcified 4.1 × 2.3 × 2.8 cm expansile lesion within the right hyoid bone

The patient has a history of melanoma and presented with a mass in the right lower lobe.
The hyoid lesion is suspected to be a synchronous primary bone tumor, such as plasmacytoma.
The hyoid lesion is suspected to be a synchronous primary bone tumor, such as chondrosarcoma.
The hyoid lesion is suspected to be a synchronous primary bone tumor, such as osteosarcoma.
The patient presented with a mass in the right lower lobe and a history of melanoma.

rationales.F08: A mass in the right lower lobe is more typical of pulmonary metastasis or a primary lung tumor like Ewing sarcoma.
rationales.F09: Malignant small round blue cell tumor is consistent with Ewing sarcoma.
rationales.F10: Molecular studies consistent with Ewing sarcoma strongly support this diagnosis.
rationales.F12: An expansile lesion in the hyoid bone could represent a primary bone tumor like plasmacytoma, chondrosarcoma, or osteosarcoma.

frontier_selector.rationale: history of melanoma and response of lung mass to chemotherapy, with hyoid lesion potentially being a second primary or unrelated lesion
